matched: topology: two closed loops touching at one common point P (the tori are tangent there, normals parallel, sin 0e+00; degenerate tangency, so the loops are tangent to each other at P, kissing, as the zoomed figure shows); appearance fitted to the Surfaces panel (silhouette, blue and orange regions, and the red loops of the result row): the orange torus' tube passes through the hole of the blue torus and rubs the wall of the hole; camera persp el=24.42 az=-78.66 roll=3.89 dist=47.800 (focal 4298 px, target at (186.6, 193.5) px) in a 437x386 panel; silhouette IoU 0.968 (blue 0.886, orange 0.882), previous construction 0.863 under its own best camera
guessed: radii and placement recovered from one view (orange R=1, r=0.56; blue R=1.1, r=0.481731516858 from the tacnode condition, ring plane tilted 109.2 deg about the line of centres); the two loops are congruent (half-turn symmetry); not reproduced: in the paper the loops are smaller and sit side by side in the blue's hole, ours wrap further round the orange tube and overlap in this view (the loop size is not a free parameter once the tori are fitted); bi-degree not stated (ours rational (2,2)); ground truth by certified continuation (trace_loops)

truth_method: certified continuation on the orange torus parameters (Newton to F = 0, every vertex within 5.6e-15 of the blue torus); the touching point P is exact
